correctness.rationale: For all a,c>=1,b>=2,q prime power, every ideal uniquely decomposes into horizontal support T, central K, and a linear lift. Pure opposite-block multiplication proves the support tensor sum dimension h=c*l+a*r-l*r. Double Möbius inversion gives the exact T multiplicity M_d; Gaussian counts of K and q^{d(ac-e)} lifts yield the displayed polynomial without overcount. Independently enumerating all row-reduced subspaces up to dimension five over F2/F3, using matrix-unit products on both sides, matched every coefficient in seven test cases. Exhaustion is only for those finite tests, not the infinite family.

evidence: Meyer–Szigeti–van Wyk describe full unital structural-ring ideals, which are blockwise when the ground ring is a field; isolated radical ideals admit non-coordinate Fq-linear graphs.
Chari–Dolbin–Ridenour characterize ad-nilpotent ideals stable under the parabolic subalgebra, whereas the current objects are ideals internal to the radical.
A complete (1,r,1) associative subalgebra census counts multiplicatively closed subspaces; the current objects require two-sided stability and allow arbitrary a and c.
Two independent complete-bipartite graphical Lie-ideal records imply precisely the b=1 special case, which this claim does not treat as novel.

originality.rationale: The novel claim is exclusively the b>=2 middle-layer amalgamation ideal polynomial; published K_{a,c} graphical Lie-ideal formulas are correctly identified as complete coverage of b=1 and excluded. The full public texts of two related ideal classifications and the (1,r,1) subalgebra census, plus 2008–2009 archival papers and 2022 class-two amalgamation theory, were compared by implications and object definitions. Their stated results neither supply nor trivially specialize to the present b>=2 finite-field coefficients. Residual general literature-priority risk remains.
residual_risks: A specialized earlier amalgamated Lie ideal-zeta computation might implicitly contain a finite-field coefficient formula although no such formula was identified in inspected material.
Other unindexed or paywalled papers were not exhaustively ruled out; historical uniqueness is not certified.

value.rationale: An exact complete ideal-dimension polynomial is a natural finite-algebra invariant controlling quotient availability and dimensions. For b>=2 central labels from several complete-bipartite blocks are identified, changing the lattice from the already covered b=1 situation. The all-characteristic all-size formula captures every non-coordinate and linked ideal by a genuine double-lattice inversion; the nontrivial case (a,b,c,q)=(2,2,1,2) has coefficient vector (1,3,19,75,651,1395,651,63,1) and total 2859.
